Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Grammar 8.3.1 Parts of Speech: Contracted Verb Forms / Positive/Negative Statements
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar 8.3.1 Parts of Speech: Contracted Verb Forms / Positive/Negative Statements, part of Strand 8 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we shorten words like cannot as can’t?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar 8.3.1 Parts of Speech: Contracted Verb Forms / Positive/Negative Statements together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: Learners develop listening or observing skill as they talk about objects in their classroom.

● Digital literacy: interacting with technology as learners use digital devices to construct sentences.

Values:
Unity: cooperation As learners work together to create a chart on contracted form of verbs.

Responsibility: determination as learner make and display a chart of contacted sentences as guided.

Link to other subjects:

Learner is able to relate the concept of verbs, positive and negative statements to their learning in Kiswahili.

  -  In pairs, learners are guided to watch a captioned video

clip or observe a signed demonstration of vocabulary

related to the farm.


  -  In pairs, learners are guided to identify, fingerspell and

sign vocabulary related to the farm.


  -  In groups, learners are guided to sign read the

following words: isn’t- is not, don’t- do not, doesn’t- does not, it’s- it is.


  -  In pairs, learners are guided to identify contracted

forms from a signed audio-visual or written text.


  -  In groups, learners are guided to categorise sample

sentences into negative or positive. learner could

display the work in a chart.


  -  In pairs, learners are guided to write contracted forms

of verbs and use them in sentences correctly.


  -  In groups, learners are guided to change positive

statements to negative statements and vice versa.


  -  In groups, learners are guided to ask each other

questions that elicit both positive and negative

answers.


  -  In pairs, learners are guided to construct positive and

negative sentences orally, through signing, and in

writing.


  -  In groups, learners are guided to make and display

charts containing contracted forms of verbs.


  -  In groups, learners are guided to use digital devices to

search for online resources on contracted verbs.
